neighbours.label: a population compared with its own past (people are healthier now, patients are waiting longer): the verb or comparative in a then-versus-now trend
fire: Compared with their grandparents, young adults today are taller and better fed.
Since 1990, homes have become larger and far more efficient.
Thanks to vaccines, children now are much less likely to die young.
Over the past decade, commuters are spending more time in traffic.
Today's retirees are wealthier and healthier than any generation before.
Since the factory closed, residents are earning less than they used to.
Compared with 1970, cars on the road are safer and cleaner.
In recent years, students are reading fewer books for pleasure.
quiet: Compared with the blue jacket, the red one is warmer and better made.
In this store, the large homes on display are made of brick.
At the clinic, children wait in a room full of toys.
On the highway this morning, commuters sat in traffic for an hour.
The retirees in our club meet every Thursday for lunch.
Near the factory, residents grow vegetables in small gardens.
Of the two cars on the lot, the grey one is safer and cleaner.
In the library, students read books quietly at long tables.

notes: Card: tops are trend statements (fat cells were now smaller, Americans are living longer, people are healthier); the output promotes comparatives (the + pole suppresses more/better/longer). Probe: trend 0.56-0.65, plain 'the cars are parked' 0.06, object-vs-object comparison 0.16.
